name: resume-hooks-silently-lost
description: Per-pane resume hooks go missing without any error — registration accepts a pane that doesn't resolve and writes a degenerate key, and valid entries are orphaned when a pane's window/pane coordinates change — so panes come back from a reboot with no resume.

bank.summary: ValidateSessionName accepts a leading -, which tmux refuses as a rename target.
bank.detail: Measured on tmux 3.7c: rename-session -t =old -bar-abc123 fails with "unknown flag -b" — the new name is a bare positional at internal/tmux/tmux.go:286 and Portal composes no -- terminator. ValidateSessionName (internal/tmux/errors.go:80) returns nil for such a name, so the TUI rename modal lets it through to a failure tmux words as a flag error. No live defect from this task — generated names only reach -s/-t optargs where a leading - is safe — but it is the same two-definitions-of-an-unwritable-name class, and this task now routes $-leading project directories into leading-hyphen names, joining the pre-existing empty-project -abc123 path. bank.summary: A period-bearing session name is unaddressable through ExactSessionTarget and is silently dropped by the capture loop — third character in this work unit own failure class. The task premise that a.b resolves both bare and exact is FALSE, and acceptance criterion 2 pins acceptance of it.
bank.detail: Measured on tmux 3.7c against isolated -L sockets. show-environment -t =a.b succeeds on a server holding only a.b, but fails with no such session: =a.b as soon as any OTHER session name is a longer prefix-extension of the pre-period component (anchor, apple reproduce; a, b, zzz do not). tmux splits a colon-free target on . into window.pane, so the session lookup is a fallback the prefix candidate displaces. Reproduced Portal-shaped: with _portal-bootstrap, my-cool-app-abc123 and user session my.app, show-environment -t =my.app exits 1 with no such session — which internal/state/capture.go:71-74 classifies as natural churn and logs as vanished, dropping a live session and its scrollback from sessions.json. has-session and kill-session fail identically. Remedy already in the codebase: tmux.ExactCoordTarget (internal/tmux/tmux.go:442, = + name + :) resolves all three correctly in every tested case. Likely fix is a per-command target-form audit of the remaining ExactSessionTarget call sites — internal/tmux/tmux.go:88,97,272,287,295,580,768 and internal/tmux/clients.go:19 — not widening the validator. Same decision should settle a leading -: rename-session -t =orig -foo fails with unknown flag -f, so a TUI rename to -foo dies on a raw tmux flag error rather than a clean refusal (loud, not silent, and pre-existing).

bank.summary: The HISTFILE=/dev/null isolation pin is defeated on this machine, and the deterministic replacement is now one line away.
bank.detail: Reviewer note, promoted so it is not lost. /etc/zshrc_Apple_Terminal (which owns .zsh_sessions and does honour SHELL_SESSIONS_DISABLE=1) is sourced by nothing under /etc on this machine, while /etc/zshrc — which every interactive zsh reads — unconditionally reassigns HISTFILE=${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zsh_history, overriding IsolateStateForTest HISTFILE=/dev/null pin and writing into the temp HOME. So the env pins are defensive rather than operative and the quiescence wait is what closes the race. The deterministic fix is cheap now that ZDOTDIR points at the temp HOME: stage a one-line .zshrc there (unset HISTFILE / SAVEHIST=0) to stop the write at source.

bank.summary: MEASURED, supersedes the earlier note on this: the isolated env shell pins are inert on this machine; the quiescence wait is carrying the whole fix, and the working lever is different from the one banked earlier.
bank.detail: Probed with a sandboxed -S server and an interactive /bin/zsh pane under a temp HOME. (a) /etc/zshrc:16 sets HISTFILE=${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zsh_history unconditionally, so the long-standing exported HISTFILE=/dev/null (internal/portaltest/isolated_env.go:43) is overridden and .zsh_history lands in the temp HOME on every run — that is the writer the teardown actually races. (b) .zsh_sessions never appeared, including with TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal and TERM_SESSION_ID set, so SHELL_SESSIONS_DISABLE=1 (:44) neutralises nothing. (c) ZDOTDIR=homeDir (:45) is a no-op by construction — ${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME} already resolves to the temp HOME. The lever that works is ZDOTDIR pointed OUTSIDE the framework TempDir tree: with it set, the probe temp HOME came back empty. (Note this differs from the earlier banked remedy of staging a .zshrc in the temp HOME.) The executor implemented the task instruction verbatim, so this is a defect in the prescription, not the execution — and the remedy reaches the pre-existing HISTFILE pin and an isolation contract every fixture inherits, so it wants its own deliberate change.

bank.summary: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED root cause: the production saver-readiness barrier fails OPEN on a fixed 2s budget — and the consequence is not only test flake but a real cold boot silently proceeding with no daemon.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/portal_saver.go:226-241 (waitForSaverDaemonReady) polls isSaverDaemonReady against saver.Readiness.Timeout, set to 2*time.Second at portal_saver.go:107. The daemon-ready INFO at :234 fires only on success, while respawn-daemon at :304 is emitted unconditionally before WaitForReady at :306 — exactly the log signature observed (respawn present, ready absent). Under the IO contention measured on this host (load 22-25 on 10 cores from fileproviderd/Dropbox/mediaanalysisd), fork+exec+flock+PID-file-write is not reliably a 2s operation. The seam is already injectable (SaverReadinessSeams, SaverOperationSeams.WaitForReady, exported at internal/tmux/export_test.go:38,63,67), so a progress-based or longer-with-hard-ceiling budget is a contained change. bank.summary: METHOD FINDING, repo-wide: go test -overlay cannot validate any source-reading guard — an overlay probe of one proves only the no-false-positive half, and the biting half passes vacuously.
bank.detail: Confirmed with a standalone module rather than by argument. A test that reads a map value at runtime AND parses its own source from disk, run under -overlay, logs RUNTIME value = OVERLAID alongside PARSED-FROM-DISK literal = original. -overlay substitutes the go command BUILD inputs; sourceguardtest.ParsePackageSources reaches disk directly (parser.ParseFile(fset, path, nil, ParseMode) with a nil src, internal/sourceguardtest/parsesources.go:50) and the test binary cwd is the real package directory. For a guard that reads parsed literals from disk AND sibling values from the compiled package it is worse than useless — an overlay makes the two halves disagree and the result is uninterpretable in either direction. CONSEQUENCE: any prior round in this phase that certified a source-reading guard by overlay should be treated as unverified. A scratch-copy edit is the sound method. This affects the ~20 sourceguardtest-driven guards and the verification habit, not any one task.
